2027-07-04.title: First Sunday of Kaitha: Feast of the Twelve Apostles
2027-07-04.readTitle: Readings of the day (First Set; mapped from the official calendar, verify locally)
readings: Elijah builds an altar of twelve stones
Many signs and wonders through the apostles
Be united in the same mind and the same purpose
Take the lowest place; invite the poor
2027-07-04.alt: Season of Kaitha (Qaita, Summer), which opens on the Sunday after the Dukhrana of St Thomas: after the apostles have sown the Gospel, the Church contemplates its growth and harvest, in the apostles, martyrs and saints who watered the Church with their blood. The Fridays of Kaitha remember martyrs and saints. The Holy Qurbana is celebrated with the Anaphora of Addai and Mari. Today is the First Sunday of Kaitha and the Feast of the Twelve Apostles, which opens the season. The calendar's own headings: “Elijah builds an altar with twelve stones”; “The Apostles heal many”; “Be united in the mind”; “The mentality of the disciple”. The calendar's longer forms are Acts 5:12–32; 1 Corinthians 1:9–16 with 2 Corinthians 1:8–14; Luke 14:1–14. In the Latin calendar today is the Fourteenth Sunday in Ordinary Time. Verify locally the times of the Holy Qurbana and how the feast is kept.
2027-07-04.verse: For all who exalt themselves will be humbled, and those who humble themselves will be exalted.
theo: After yesterday's Dukhrana of Mar Thoma, our Church turns today to all twelve. “He called his disciples and chose twelve of them, whom he also named apostles”, Luke says, after a night on the mountain “in prayer to God”. Their names are given in the Gospels in four lists, and the first is this: “These are the names of the twelve apostles: first, Simon, also known as Peter, and his brother Andrew; James son of Zebedee, and his brother John; Philip and Bartholomew; Thomas and Matthew the tax collector; James son of Alphaeus, and Thaddaeus; Simon the Cananaean, and Judas Iscariot, the one who betrayed him.” Mark gives the purpose: “And he appointed twelve, whom he also named apostles, to be with him, and to be sent out to proclaim the message.” First to be with him, then to be sent. The number is deliberate: twelve, like the tribes of Israel, because Jesus was gathering the whole people of God anew. “You who have followed me will also sit on twelve thrones, judging the twelve tribes of Israel.” After the betrayal of Judas, the apostles prayed and “the lot fell on Matthias; and he was added to the eleven apostles”: the Twelve is a college that the Church keeps whole (CCC 880). In the last book of the Bible the holy city has “twelve foundations, and on them are the twelve names of the twelve apostles of the Lamb”. Today we keep the feast of all the names, including those about whom the Gospels tell us almost nothing; they too are foundation stones.

Today also opens the Season of Kaitha, the summer of the Church's year. After the apostles have sown, the Church looks at the growth and the harvest. The first reading chooses a very fitting beginning: a prophet builds an altar. In the days of King Ahab, Israel was “limping with two different opinions”, between the Lord and Baal, and the altar of the Lord on Mount Carmel “had been thrown down”. “Then Elijah said to all the people, ‘Come closer to me’; and all the people came closer to him. First he repaired the altar of the Lord that had been thrown down; Elijah took twelve stones, according to the number of the tribes of the sons of Jacob, to whom the word of the Lord came, saying, ‘Israel shall be your name’; with the stones he built an altar in the name of the Lord.” Twelve stones, one altar: the divided people is gathered again, and the Lord's name is the name above the whole. Elijah has the sacrifice soaked with water three times, so that whatever follows can only be the Lord's doing, and his prayer is short and humble: “Answer me, O Lord, answer me, so that this people may know that you, O Lord, are God, and that you have turned their hearts back.” Then “the fire of the Lord fell and consumed the burnt offering, the wood, the stones, and the dust, and even licked up the water that was in the trench.” The people fall on their faces: “The Lord indeed is God; the Lord indeed is God.” The Church has always seen in the twelve stones the twelve apostles, on whom the new altar of the Church is built; and in the fire from heaven the fire of Pentecost, which made the same twelve a witness.

The Acts reading shows what the fire did. “Now many signs and wonders were done among the people through the apostles. And they were all together in Solomon’s Portico.” They stayed in the Temple, as faithful sons of Israel; the Church did not begin by leaving the house of the Lord but by praying in it. The people held them in high esteem, and “more than ever believers were added to the Lord, great numbers of both men and women, so that they even carried out the sick into the streets, and laid them on cots and mats, in order that Peter’s shadow might fall on some of them as he came by. A great number of people would also gather from the towns around Jerusalem, bringing the sick and those tormented by unclean spirits, and they were all cured.” This is harvest. Then the high priest and the party of the Sadducees, “being filled with jealousy”, arrested the apostles and put them in the public prison. We see here one group of leaders, the high priest and his party, and not the Jewish people, who held the apostles in high esteem. “But during the night an angel of the Lord opened the prison doors, brought them out, and said, ‘Go, stand in the temple and tell the people the whole message about this life.’” An open prison door and a command to go back to the very place of danger: the Church is sent, again and again, to speak the whole message and not only the parts that are welcome.

Paul, writing to Corinth, shows what can happen to a Church that forgets the one Lord. “God is faithful; by him you were called into the fellowship of his Son, Jesus Christ our Lord. Now I appeal to you, brothers and sisters, by the name of our Lord Jesus Christ, that all of you be in agreement and that there be no divisions among you, but that you be united in the same mind and the same purpose.” The Corinthians were each saying, “I belong to Paul,” or “I belong to Apollos,” or “I belong to Cephas,” or “I belong to Christ.” The apostles, great as they were, are never meant to be the names of parties. Paul answers with three questions: “Has Christ been divided? Was Paul crucified for you? Or were you baptized in the name of Paul?” The Twelve are many, and the Lord is one. This is also a prayer for our own day: for the unity of our parishes and our Church, and for the unity of all who are baptised into Christ, with the Orthodox, the Mar Thoma and the Malankara Churches, who also honour the apostles and share much of our heritage. “There is one body and one Spirit, just as you were called to the one hope of your calling, one Lord, one faith, one baptism” (Ephesians 4:4–5; CCC 813).

The Gospel is set at a meal. Jesus is at table in the house of a leading Pharisee, and he sees how the guests choose the places of honour. He tells them a parable: “When you are invited by someone to a wedding banquet, do not sit down at the place of honor… But when you are invited, go and sit down at the lowest place, so that when your host comes, he may say to you, ‘Friend, move up higher’; then you will be honored in the presence of all who sit at the table with you.” The principle is the one that should rule the Church: “For all who exalt themselves will be humbled, and those who humble themselves will be exalted.” The apostles themselves had to learn it. At the Last Supper “a dispute also arose among them as to which one of them was to be regarded as the greatest,” and Jesus answered, “the greatest among you must become like the youngest, and the leader like one who serves… I am among you as one who serves.” Then he turns to the host: “When you give a luncheon or a dinner, do not invite your friends or your brothers or your relatives or rich neighbors, in case they may invite you in return… But when you give a banquet, invite the poor, the crippled, the lame, and the blind. And you will be blessed, because they cannot repay you, for you will be repaid at the resurrection of the righteous.” In Kerala this is the parish feast, with its nercha meal: let the first to be served and the best seat be for the one who cannot give anything back. In this season of the harvest the rice-ears that are full bow their heads, and the empty ones stand straight. The Twelve, humbled by their failure and lifted by the Spirit, are the ears that bowed.
conn: “Now during those days he went out to the mountain to pray; and he spent the night in prayer to God. And when day came, he called his disciples and chose twelve of them, whom he also named apostles” (Luke 6:12–13).
“And he appointed twelve, whom he also named apostles, to be with him, and to be sent out to proclaim the message” (Mark 3:14).
“Go therefore and make disciples of all nations, baptizing them in the name of the Father and of the Son and of the Holy Spirit” (Matthew 28:19).
“You did not choose me but I chose you. And I appointed you to go and bear fruit, fruit that will last” (John 15:16).

“May those who sow in tears reap with shouts of joy. Those who go out weeping, bearing the seed for sowing, shall come home with shouts of joy, carrying their sheaves” (Psalm 126:5–6); “so that sower and reaper may rejoice together” (John 4:36).
“whoever wishes to be great among you must be your servant” (Matthew 20:26); “Humble yourselves before the Lord, and he will exalt you” (James 4:10).
“that they may all be one. As you, Father, are in me and I am in you, may they also be in us, so that the world may believe that you have sent me” (John 17:21).
outline: The Twelve and the opening of Kaitha: from sowing to harvest.
The names of the Twelve, chosen after prayer; Elijah's altar; the fire from heaven.
Point 2 · Go and tell the whole message
Signs in the Temple; Peter's shadow; the open prison door; the harvest of the Church.
Not I belong to Paul or Cephas, but all belong to Christ; unity with one another and among the Churches.
Point 4 · The lowest place and the empty chair
Humility at the banquet; the apostles who argued and learned; the parish feast and the poor.
“All who humble themselves will be exalted.”
live: Learn the names of the Twelve this week and say them with your family at evening prayer; add the name of Matthias.
At the next parish gathering, a feast, a meeting or a meal, take the last seat and serve someone else first.
If your family keeps a feast this month, invite one person who cannot invite you back, and sit with them.
fathers: The other apostles were what Peter was, sharing an equal fellowship of honour and power; but the beginning starts from unity, so that the Church of Christ may be shown to be one.
Do you want to build a great tower of holiness? Think first of the foundation of humility. The higher you intend to raise the building, the deeper you must dig the foundation.
magis: When Christ instituted the Twelve, he made them a college or permanent assembly and put Peter at its head. The college of bishops, with the Pope as its head, is the continuation of the college of apostles.

The Church is one because of her source, the unity of the Trinity; because of her founder, Christ; and because of her soul, the Holy Spirit. Her unity is a gift, and we must keep it with every effort.
saints: First Sunday of Kaitha, the Feast of the Twelve Apostles. In the Latin calendar, the Fourteenth Sunday in Ordinary Time.
Mon 5 and Tue 6: the first Monday and Tuesday of Kaitha; Tue 6 also St Maria Goretti. Fri 9 July: First Friday of Kaitha, St James of Nisibis.
2027-07-04.prayer: Lord Jesus Christ, you prayed all night and chose twelve to be with you and to be sent. We thank you for Peter and Andrew, James and John, Philip and Bartholomew, Thomas and Matthew, James and Thaddaeus, Simon and Matthias. As you built an altar of twelve stones in the days of Elijah, build your Church on the foundation of the apostles, with yourself as cornerstone. Send the fire of your Spirit on us at the opening of this season; keep us one in mind and purpose; teach us to take the lowest place, to invite the poor, and to bring a rich harvest for your kingdom. You live and reign with the Father and the Holy Spirit, one God, for ever. Amen.
altar: At the Holy Qurbana the altar is the place where the fire of heaven falls on the offering. Elijah's altar of twelve stones is a sign of ours: the altar of the Church rests on the apostles, and the Lord himself is the cornerstone. When the priest calls down the Holy Spirit on the bread and wine, we ask for the fire that fell on Carmel and on the Upper Room, and the people answer as they did on Carmel: “The Lord indeed is God.” The words of the Last Supper, handed on by the apostles, are the words we hear at every Qurbana.

And this altar is a banquet table where the first places belong to the poor: the Lord who made himself the servant of the Twelve at the Last Supper serves us with his own Body and Blood. Those who come to this table as beggars leave as brothers and sisters, and take their seat with the lowest and the last.

quick: The Feast of the Twelve Apostles opens the Season of Kaitha: the apostles sowed the Gospel, and the Church now contemplates its growth and harvest.
Elijah rebuilds the altar with twelve stones and the fire of the Lord falls; the people say, “The Lord indeed is God.”
The apostles do many signs; an angel opens the prison and sends them back to teach in the Temple. Paul: Christ is not divided; be united in the same mind.
Jesus: take the lowest place at the banquet, and invite those who cannot repay you.
2027-07-04.action: Learn the names of the Twelve this week and pray them at evening prayer; at the next parish meal, take the last seat.
2027-07-04.question: Where am I looking for the seat of honour, and where is the Lord asking me to sit lower?
kidsaint: Jesus had twelve special friends, called apostles: Peter, Andrew, James, John, Philip, Bartholomew, Thomas, Matthew, James, Thaddaeus, Simon, and Judas, who was later replaced by Matthias. They were fishermen, a tax collector and ordinary working people. Jesus asked them to be with him and then to go and tell everyone about God. They did not always understand, and once they even argued about who was the greatest! But Jesus taught them to serve, and the Holy Spirit made them brave. Lesson: you do not have to be perfect to be Jesus' friend. Say yes, stay close to him, and then go and tell others!
2027-07-04.special: First Sunday of Kaitha and Feast of the Twelve Apostles: the season of Kaitha (summer) begins.
term: The Syriac word for an apostle means one who is sent. Our Malayalam word ശ്ലീഹാ comes from it. The Twelve were first called to be with Jesus and then sent out. The season that has just ended is called the Season of the Apostles (ശ്ലീഹാക്കാലം). Kaitha (Qaita), the season that begins today, means summer.

family.explain: Jesus once saw people at a dinner hurrying to take the best seats. He said: when you are invited, sit in the last place; then the host may say, ‘Friend, come up higher!’ He also said: when you have a feast, invite people who have nothing and cannot give you anything back, and God will bless you. Today the Church remembers Jesus' twelve special friends, the apostles. They learned to serve and not to push for the best place. When we do small things for others, we are like the apostles.
family.intention: We pray for our parish, our priests, and all who help to prepare the feast, and for people who go hungry or who sit alone.
family.ask: Ask: “Who can we invite to share a meal this month, someone who cannot invite us back?”

illus: In a hill parish in Idukki (a story told to illustrate the reading) the feast of the church was always a big meal after the Qurbana. The front benches were kept for the guests of honour, and the old catechist Mathai, who had taught three generations, always came late from his field and stood at the back. One year the new priest, noticing him, stopped in the middle of the announcements. ‘Mathai chettan, there is a seat here.’ Mathai smiled and said, ‘Achen, I am comfortable at the back.’ The priest said, ‘Then let us all move to the back.’ And the whole church laughed and made room, and the priest sat down on the last bench himself. That year, for the first time, the feast meal was served first to the old people and the children and to the families that had no money to give, and the guests of honour waited and were served last, and nobody remembered the seating afterwards. They remembered how happy the whole parish was.

pm.open: Lord Jesus, you called the Twelve to be with you and to be sent. Gather us now as your friends, and send us out again with your Spirit. Amen.
share: Elijah took twelve stones (1 Kings 18:31). What stones, what people and what truths is my life built on?
Go, stand in the temple and tell the people the whole message (Acts 5:20). Do I tell only the welcome parts of the Gospel, or the whole?
Has Christ been divided? (1 Corinthians 1:13). Where in my family or parish do I take sides, and what would it take to be one?
Go and sit down at the lowest place (Luke 14:10). Where am I choosing the places of honour?
pm.resp: Lord, make us one in you.
interc: For the Pope, our Major Archbishop, our bishops and all the successors of the apostles, that they may be servants of unity.
For our parishes, that they may be places where the lowest place is loved and the poor are first at the table.
For the unity of all Christians, especially with the Churches that share the heritage of Saint Thomas.
For farmers and for those who work in the fields in this monsoon season, and for a good harvest.
For young people who are being called by Jesus, that they may answer.
pm.close: Father, you built your Church on the foundation of the apostles. As we begin this season of growth and harvest, keep us united in mind and purpose, humble in heart, and generous to the poor, so that we may bring forth fruit that lasts. Through Christ our Lord. Amen.

homily: Dear friends, today is the First Sunday of Kaitha, and our Church celebrates the Feast of the Twelve Apostles. Yesterday we remembered Mar Thoma. Today we remember all the twelve friends of Jesus. “He called his disciples and chose twelve of them, whom he also named apostles” (Luke 6:13).

In the first reading the prophet Elijah builds an altar. He takes twelve stones, one for each tribe of Israel, and the people are one again before the Lord. Then the fire falls from heaven and the people say, “The Lord indeed is God” (1 Kings 18:39). The Church has always seen in those twelve stones the twelve apostles, on whom the altar of our Church is built, and in the fire the fire of the Holy Spirit at Pentecost.

In the Acts the apostles are very busy and very happy. Many people are healed, and more and more believe. The authorities arrest them, but during the night an angel opens the prison and says, “Go, stand in the temple and tell the people the whole message about this life” (Acts 5:20). The Church is sent to say all of the message, not just the parts that are pleasant to hear.

Saint Paul tells the Corinthians that some say, “I belong to Paul”, and others “I belong to Apollos” or “to Cephas”. He asks, “Has Christ been divided?” (1 Corinthians 1:13). The Twelve are many, but Christ is one. Let us pray for unity in our families and parishes, and among all who are baptised in Christ.

In the Gospel Jesus is a guest at a meal and sees people choosing the best seats. He says: sit in the lowest place, “for all who exalt themselves will be humbled, and those who humble themselves will be exalted” (Luke 14:11). And invite the poor, the crippled, the lame and the blind, who cannot pay you back. The apostles themselves once argued about who was the greatest, and Jesus taught them to serve. In the Kaitha season the full ears of rice bow down. Let us bow, too: let us take the last seat, serve first the one who cannot repay us, and so bring fruit that will last. Amen.
kids: Children, today we remember Jesus' twelve special friends, the apostles. Jesus asked them first to be with him, and then to go and tell everyone about God. They were ordinary people: fishermen, farmers and a tax collector.

Jesus also teaches us today: do not rush for the best seat. Take the last seat and let your friend sit first! And when you have a party, invite someone who is alone. That is how the apostles learned to love, and that is how we can too!

On the First Sunday of Kaitha, the Feast of the Twelve Apostles: twelve stones and one altar, the open prison door, the one Christ who is not divided, and the lowest place at the banquet.

concl: The Church is built on the Twelve, like Elijah's altar on twelve stones, and she is sent to tell the whole message.
Christ is not divided; let us be one in mind and purpose, take the lowest place, and invite those who cannot repay us.
